To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the presence of PVA in the ternary blended pasting increases the hydration rate of PC at early ages and reduces the CH content.
the amount of CH in PC-PFA blended systems increased up to three-days and then it progressively decreased and the reduction was proportional to PFA dosage.
the amount of CH increases with age in binary blended pastes and decreases with the addition of SF.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an accurate and efficient approach to predict the age-dependent hydration of cementitious systems.
the hydration of blended cement systems using TGA and SEM techniques.
the development of a new method to assess the hydration of blended cementitious systems and the microstructural development of blended cementitious system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hydration of ternary blended systems containing PFA and SF is more complex and the hydration parameters cannot be simply predicted using binary blended systems.

the hydration development of PC-PFA-SF ternary blended systems was found to be more complex and the hydration parameters (CH, water and porosity) were found to be more interrelated compared to PC-PFA systems.
the presence of PVA and SF in PC pastes has significantly altered the hydration development of blended systems and the microstructure evolution of the cementitious matrix.
